title: Side chair by Hector Guimard
lede: A pearwood chair whose back posts rise, split, and flow into a leaf-shaped leather panel, with no joint or edge left straight.
summary: Pearwood chair with a pointed leaf-shaped leather back and flowing carved posts. Hector Guimard, Paris, c. 1907.

evidence.note: Downloaded and inspected the Cleveland Museum of Art open-access image of object 1985.96 (2272 × 3400 px print file). Read the object record through the museum’s open-access API.

styles.note: Paris Art Nouveau furniture by the designer of the Métro entrances: the frame reads as one carved plant stem that divides and joins.

context: The Cleveland Museum of Art records the chair as pearwood with a tooled leather back and seat, 108 × 45.4 × 50.4 cm, French, c. 1907, by Hector Guimard (1867–1942). [CMA 1985.96](https://clevelandart.org/art/1985.96).

Wikipedia: after visiting Horta’s [Hôtel Tassel](ref:horta-hotel-tassel-staircase-1893), Guimard built the Castel Béranger (1895–1898), among the first Paris buildings in the new style, and his [Métro entrances](ref:guimard-paris-metro-entrance-1900) brought it to the visitors of the 1900 Exposition. [Wikipedia: Art Nouveau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_Nouveau).
observed: The back is a pointed, inverted-triangle shield with curved sides, filled with a brown leather panel edged by a row of brass nails.
The two back posts swell as they rise, bend inward, and merge into the top rail; carved grooves run along them like the veins of a stem.
A single central splat drops from the back panel, splits into a narrow pointed opening, and joins the seat rail.
The front seat rail dips in the middle and carries a small carved scroll ornament.
The legs taper and flare slightly into small pad feet. No edge on the frame is straight.
The photograph shows the chair in three-quarter view on a gray ground.
interpretation: The chair turns the rubric’s leaf-shaped panel into structure: the back is literally a leaf held up by its stalk.
The palette is only wood brown, leather brown, and brass, which fits the style’s earthy colours.
borrow: Shape a card or badge as a pointed shield with softly curved sides.
Carry a thin groove or line along a curved edge so the edge reads as a stem.

images.alt: Tall wooden side chair on a gray ground, in three-quarter view. The back is a pointed leaf shape filled with brown leather and edged with brass nails, carried on curved carved posts, above a brown leather seat.
images.caption: Hector Guimard, chair, c. 1907, pearwood and tooled leather. [Cleveland Museum of Art 1985.96](https://clevelandart.org/art/1985.96), CC0.

rights.statement: The Cleveland Museum of Art marks the object and its image CC0. Hector Guimard died in 1942, so his work entered the public domain in France in 2013. A chair made about 1907 is in the public domain in the United States. The Met, by contrast, marks its Guimard objects as not public domain; this record relies on Cleveland’s CC0 statement and the author’s death date.
